heading: Architecting Frida Instrumentation for In-Memory Payload Extraction
core_technical_idea: Early-stage Frida instrumentation lifecycle showing how native Python process control and JS runtime hooks intercept in-memory DEX bytes at the ClassLoader boundary before execution.
must_show: Python Host Harness lifecycle (spawn, attach, load, resume)
Frida JS agent injection into Android Runtime (ART)
IPC byte array transfer via send() message payload
SHA-256 calculation and DEX file persistence to local disk
composition: Sequence diagram progressing left-to-right from Host Python runner to Frida Agent, target ART Process, and local file storage.
alt_text: Sequence diagram illustrating early instrumentation dynamic analysis, showing Frida Python spawner, JS runtime hook on ClassLoader.defineClass, raw byte extraction, IPC messaging, and DEX file writing.
caption: Interception sequence showing early process attachment, ClassLoader hooking, and asynchronous buffer extraction to host disk before bytecode execution.
mermaid_code:
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant Host as Host Python Harness
    participant Frida as Frida JS Runtime
    participant ART as Android Runtime (Target PID)
    participant Disk as Host Disk Storage

    Host->>ART: device.spawn([PACKAGE_NAME])
    Host->>Frida: create_script(javascript_code) & script.load()
    Frida->>ART: Overload ClassLoader.defineClass(name, b, offset, length)
    Host->>ART: device.resume(PID)
    
    Note over ART: App unpacking sequence triggers dynamic DEX loading
    
    ART->>Frida: Invoke defineClass(name, byte[], offset, length)
    activate Frida
    Frida->>Frida: Memory.readByteArray(b.rawPointer + offset, length)
    Frida->>Host: send({type: 'dex_dump'}, buffer)
    Frida->>ART: Execute original this.defineClass(...)
    deactivate Frida
    
    activate Host
    Host->>Host: Compute SHA-256 of extracted buffer
    Host->>Disk: Write payload_{sha256[:12]}.dex
    deactivate Host

heading: Failure-Mode Analysis of Memory Dumps and Timing Attacks
core_technical_idea: Multi-threaded race conditions and GC collisions during dynamic instrumentation cause crashes unless memory operations are offloaded asynchronously.
must_show: Native worker threads invoking defineClass simultaneously
ART Garbage Collection memory sweep collision
Unmitigated path leading to SIGSEGV crash
Mitigated path using Memory.dup() and an async queue
composition: Two-path comparison flowchart: Left path shows target thread contention colliding with synchronous Frida callbacks and ART GC sweeps leading to SIGSEGV; Right path shows fast native heap copying via Memory.dup() feeding an async queue to maintain thread stability.
alt_text: Flowchart comparing unmitigated multi-threaded instrumentation failure modes against the Memory.dup asynchronous queue mitigation strategy.
caption: Synchronous memory logging creates lock contention and GC races; offloading buffer allocation via Memory.dup() prevents SIGSEGV crashes.

flowchart TD
    subgraph Target [Target Process Execution]
        T1[Worker Thread A: defineClass]
        T2[Worker Thread B: defineClass]

        SyncHook[Synchronous JS Callback]

    end

    subgraph Mitigated [Mitigated Hook: Safe Path]
